notes: ui-ux-pro-max is a model-invocable design-intelligence skill: style/color/font selection, UX and accessibility review, interaction/layout planning across web and mobile. Evals verify it applies the priority rule categories and Quick Reference (accessibility 4.5:1, touch 44x44, semantic tokens), the product-type style guide, and the AI anti-pattern list and pre-delivery checklist. Per its own routing table it runs BEFORE design-screen/ui-styling, so an implementation request is not a mis-fire; the genuine boundary is its Skip clause (pure backend/API/DB/infra/DevOps).

evals.prompt: Help me choose a style, color palette, and font pairing for a healthcare patient dashboard.
evals.expected_output: Uses the product-type -> style guide (healthcare: clean/accessible, soft teal + white, Lato/Source Sans) to recommend a style, a WCAG-compliant palette with semantic tokens, and a heading/body font pairing — checking contrast (4.5:1), dark-mode pairing, and steering clear of the AI anti-patterns (mesh gradients, glassmorphism-everywhere, emoji icons).

evals.prompt: Review this signup form's UI for accessibility and UX problems before we ship.
evals.expected_output: Audits against the CRITICAL/HIGH rule categories: contrast ratio, visible labels (not placeholder-only), error placement below the field, touch-target size and spacing, keyboard/focus states, and required-field indicators — flagging violations and running the pre-delivery checklist (accessibility / interaction / layout / typography-color).

evals.prompt: Design the database schema and REST API for our orders service.
evals.expected_output: Should route to database-design / not fire, because ui-ux-pro-max's Skip clause excludes pure backend logic, API, and database design — nothing here changes how a feature looks, feels, moves, or is interacted with.
